inspection_summary: Inspected all 2,234 Python splitlines from title through references. The source develops an inverse-designed unitary single-plaquette model whose resolvent is built from the symmetric zeta function, derives logarithmic eigenvalue-density spikes and potential jumps at mapped nontrivial zeros, rewrites the model through symmetric-group characters and dominant Young diagrams, and proposes free-fermion phase-space and prime-counting correspondences. Thirty-four source-grounded units retain the reusable mechanisms, explicit qualifications, and appendix checks. Formula extraction is mostly readable but several conclusions are equation- and figure-dependent; the source itself conditions key resolvent analyticity on RH and calls theta=pi*u(h) heuristic rather than proved.

accepted_units.title: From spectral analogies to a Young-diagram phase space
accepted_units.why_material: Connects Hilbert-Polya and random-matrix analogies to the paper's concrete plan: model eigenangles as positions, Young-row lengths as momenta, and use their relation to draw a zero-sensitive phase space.
accepted_units.context_note: Historical similarity is motivation, not validation; the operative construction begins with the position/momentum dual descriptions in lines 122-145.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant; the critical-line notation is recoverable from text despite symbol extraction noise.

accepted_units.title: Inverse model design with divergences rather than a zero density
accepted_units.why_material: Precisely distinguishes the proposed observable: a no-gap eigenvalue density has logarithmic divergences at mapped zeros, but is not itself identified with the zero distribution.
accepted_units.context_note: This distinction constrains every later claim about what the matrix model captures.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The partition function is formula-dependent, while the divergence-versus-distribution distinction is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Universality question for free-fermion large-N saddles
accepted_units.why_material: Frames the eigenvalue/Young duality as a universality problem and states that extremization, rather than an accidental identification, should produce the h-theta relation for generic plaquette phases.
accepted_units.context_note: The universality claim is limited by the authors to the class of one-plaquette models and proposed extensions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded; no missing formula is needed for the conceptual claim.

accepted_units.title: Arbitrary-cycle characters block direct Young-density solution
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies the technical obstruction—no tractable exact arbitrary-cycle character—and the weaker but sufficient target of deriving a boundary relation between row lengths and eigenangles.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly does not claim to compute the complete dominant Young distribution generically.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded; notation hi and theta_i is locally explained.

accepted_units.title: Generic Fourier-coupled unitary one-plaquette model
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the parameterized action whose Fourier couplings control phases and later become Li-number coefficients.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the common model substrate for the eigenvalue and representation descriptions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation-dependent but legible; trace, Haar measure, and Taylor/Fourier coefficients should be preserved.

accepted_units.title: Eigenangle saddle equation with Haar repulsion
accepted_units.why_material: Shows the reusable move from a unitary integral to a continuum eigenvalue density governed by an external Fourier force and cotangent repulsion.
accepted_units.context_note: The final singular-integral equation is the comparison target for the character saddle in section 5.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy; text extraction retains the saddle's structure, but scan verification is advisable before equation-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Resolvent analyticity, reciprocal symmetry, and Dyson-Schwinger closure
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces a singular integral by an analytic function inside and outside the unit disk, with R(z)+R(1/z)=1 and a quadratic Dyson-Schwinger solution controlling phases.
accepted_units.context_note: The displayed general F(z) expansion is extraction-dense; the reliable reusable content is the analytic domains, reciprocal relation, and algebraic closure.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strong equation dependency and formula-layout risk in lines 421-475; verify against the scan for exact coefficients.

accepted_units.title: Density and force as resolvent boundary components
accepted_units.why_material: Gives the bridge from the analytic resolvent to eigenvalue density via its jump/real part and to the potential derivative via its imaginary part.
accepted_units.context_note: These identities drive both the spike-density and step-potential constructions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Compact equations are legible; epsilon and real/imaginary symbols show text-layer encoding noise.

accepted_units.title: Completed zeta as an entire involution-symmetric input
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces xi(s), removes the pole/trivial-zero singularities, and supplies xi(s)=xi(1-s), the symmetry later translated into the resolvent reciprocal condition.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit records the source's normalization convention and analytic claim without importing outside properties.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation-dependent; gamma and real typography are readable but should be scan-checked for exact normalization.

accepted_units.title: Prime product and zero product representations
accepted_units.why_material: Places the prime and nontrivial-zero factorizations side by side, enabling the later density calculation and prime-counting comparison.
accepted_units.context_note: The source uses the xi zero product as the direct input to the logarithmic density.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent and normalization-sensitive; retain source convention and verify before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Li coefficients as derivative data and a zero sum
accepted_units.why_material: States RH equivalence to nonnegativity of all Li coefficients and supplies both the derivative definition and zero-based expression used as model couplings.
accepted_units.context_note: This criterion is later re-expressed through the constructed resolvent; that later argument inherits its assumptions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent; powers, factorials, and zero indexing are recoverable but merit scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Mapping the critical line to the unit circle
accepted_units.why_material: Uses s=1/(1-z) to map the critical line to |z|=1, separates the two half-planes by the circle, and transfers zero accumulation and xi symmetry into the unit-disk geometry.
accepted_units.context_note: Placement of every nontrivial zero on the circle is explicitly conditional on RH in the source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The map and t-theta relation are equation-dependent but textually clear; figure 1 is supplementary.

accepted_units.title: Resolvent designed from log xi
accepted_units.why_material: Constructs inside/outside branches of R from log xi, fixes normalization at z=0, enforces reciprocal symmetry, and exposes logarithmic branch points at mapped zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly says inside-disk analyticity assumes RH and acknowledges other admissible resolvents; this is a selected design, not uniqueness.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation- and branch-choice-dependent; extraction is readable, but exact signs and arguments require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Normalized no-gap density with zero-marked logarithmic spikes
accepted_units.why_material: Expands the xi product into a density whose logarithmic divergences occur at mapped zero angles while remaining integrable and normalized across the full circle.
accepted_units.context_note: The density encodes zeros through singularities and includes a separate accumulation divergence at theta=0; it is not a sum of delta masses.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula and figure dependent; prose recovers the spike/no-gap mechanism, while exact log-sine coefficients need scan checking.

accepted_units.title: Li numbers as plaquette couplings
accepted_units.why_material: Matches Taylor coefficients of the designed no-gap resolvent to Cauchy representations of Li numbers, producing beta_n=-alpha*lambda_n/n and an explicit matrix action.
accepted_units.context_note: The equality uses the no-gap Dyson-Schwinger branch and the source's xi and Li normalization conventions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strong equation dependency; contour factors, signs, and n-powers must be verified against the scan before computational use.

accepted_units.title: Zero crossings become jumps in the potential derivative
accepted_units.why_material: Tracks the imaginary part of log xi across upper- and lower-half-plane zeros to obtain a step function and hence discrete force jumps at mapped zero positions.
accepted_units.context_note: This provides an independent consistency view of the same designed action through the imaginary resolvent component.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Branch conventions and extracted imaginary-part symbols are fragile; prose supports the mechanism, exact equations require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Resolvent boundary data yields a nonnegative Li cosine sum
accepted_units.why_material: Fourier extraction plus integration by parts converts Li coefficients into a sum of terms 1-cos(n theta_i), making positivity manifest inside the proposed unit-circle construction.
accepted_units.context_note: This is not independent RH evidence: the earlier resolvent analyticity and placement of all zeros on the unit circle were explicitly assumed under RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent; the final cosine sum is legible, but normalization and integration equations should be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: From trace powers to a sum over Young diagrams
accepted_units.why_material: Expands the plaquette exponential by cycle counts, decomposes trace monomials into symmetric-group characters, uses U(N) character orthogonality, and recasts the partition function as a representation sum.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the algebraic bridge that permits a momentum-like Young description of the same model.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly notation- and equation-dependent; character labels, cycle constraints, and normalization factors should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Young density and constant-density droplet marginals
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the large-N row variable and Young density, then formulates eigenvalue and Young densities as marginals of one constant phase-space distribution whose boundary carries the phase information.
accepted_units.context_note: The simple-model identification motivates the generic derivation; the source says its earlier appearance was accidental.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations are central; one extracted u(u) likely denotes u(h), so exact notation needs scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Frobenius coefficient formula for arbitrary cycle data
accepted_units.why_material: Provides the available exact character representation for arbitrary conjugacy classes through power sums, a Vandermonde factor, and coefficient extraction.
accepted_units.context_note: The formula is exact in principle but does not itself make the large-N arbitrary-cycle character easy to evaluate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strong formula-layout dependency; coefficient subscripts and products require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Frobenius auxiliary variables recover the eigenvalue saddle and boundary
accepted_units.why_material: Exponentiates the Frobenius contour integral, takes a large-N saddle on the unit circle, identifies its imaginary part with the eigenvalue equation, and obtains a real algebraic relation between h and theta.
accepted_units.context_note: The identification n*k'_n/Z_n=beta_n is justified at partition level in the following section, so this unit should be read with u23.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very formula-heavy with control-character artifacts; scan verification is required for exact actions, measures, and factors.

accepted_units.title: Even-function redundancy in the Young boundary equation
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that the character action cannot distinguish h(theta) from h(theta)+f(theta) for even f, so different Young distributions can correspond to the same eigenvalue density.
accepted_units.context_note: The redundancy is subsequently constrained by requiring a constant-density phase-space topology.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose conclusion is clear; the action and boundary equation are extraction-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Partition-level identification of auxiliary variables with eigenvalues
accepted_units.why_material: Extremizes the full representation integral, obtains conjugate unit-circle saddle variables, fixes cycle counts by Fourier moments, and recovers the original eigenvalue partition function.
accepted_units.context_note: This supplies the promised justification for using Frobenius auxiliary angles as the model's eigenangles at large N.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Dense multi-line equations and measures are extraction-risky; the partition-equivalence conclusion is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: No-gap and multi-gap topology fix boundary separation
accepted_units.why_material: Constrains the boundary redundancy by droplet topology: a no-gap phase has boundaries 0 and 2*pi*rho, while a multi-gap phase has two nonzero boundaries separated by 2*pi*rho.
accepted_units.context_note: The source defers a complete Young-distribution construction and relies on the later theta=pi*u(h) identification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation-dependent; the qualitative topological cases are recoverable, exact factors should be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: Complex phase-space distribution combines density and potential
accepted_units.why_material: Defines Omega(h,theta) so its real marginal gives eigenvalue density, its imaginary marginal gives the potential derivative, and its theta marginal gives Young density; real topology varies by phase while imaginary topology is model-fixed.
accepted_units.context_note: This extends the constant real droplet to a complex bookkeeping device rather than a conventional positive probability density.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent; an extracted argument q in line 1672 appears inconsistent with theta and should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: One spiky density supports multiple normalized Young representations
accepted_units.why_material: Applies the no-gap boundary to the Riemann-zero density and explains how nonmonotonicity yields multiple monotone branches and hence multiple dominant representations for the same eigenvalue distribution.
accepted_units.context_note: The branch examples depend on figure 4 and use normalization to fix constants; they do not enumerate a complete generic solution.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Figure- and equation-dependent; the prose clearly states the non-one-to-one mechanism.

accepted_units.title: Broom-shaped zero phase space
accepted_units.why_material: Interprets positive h radially and periodic theta angularly, turning density spikes into sticks positioned at mapped Riemann zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a qualitative geometry read from the no-gap boundary and figure 5, not a new zero theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Figure 5 is essential for detailed geometry; prose preserves the broom/stick interpretation.

accepted_units.title: Prime-counting fluctuation as an alternative phase-space variable
accepted_units.why_material: Uses the prime-counting function and its Mellin relation to log zeta to rewrite the same resolvent through a distribution over the fluctuating prime-counting component J-tilde.
accepted_units.context_note: The source presents a similarity with the h representation; it does not establish equality of the two phase spaces.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extremely formula-sensitive with damaged tilde placement and limits; scan verification is required before exact mathematical reuse.

accepted_units.title: Non-injective Young/prime correspondence and canonical-transform suggestion
accepted_units.why_material: Compares the many inverse branches of J-tilde to the multiple Young branches, proposes h corresponding to J-tilde and u(h) to an inverse-x quantity, and suggests—but does not prove—a canonical relation.
accepted_units.context_note: The paper labels this as resemblance and future work; Fourier-transform language is offered as suggestive evidence only.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose carries the qualification, while exact mapped variables are tilde- and exponent-sensitive and need scan checking.

accepted_units.title: Limits of the free-fermion interpretation
accepted_units.why_material: Separates the classical large-N droplet from a still-unknown quantum many-body theory, notes compact group-manifold and trigonometric-boundary differences, and explicitly says theta=pi*u(h) is unproved.
accepted_units.context_note: These qualifications bound the source's universality and physical-interpretation claims.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded; no formula reconstruction is needed.

accepted_units.title: Replace logarithmic spikes by an exact zero-counting density
accepted_units.why_material: Proposes a sharper follow-up model whose density is the derivative of the zero-counting step function, to retest the Young/prime relation when eigenvalues are concentrated directly at zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The source records this as future work, not a completed model or observed result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The delta-density equation is legible but distributional notation should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Product formula to log-sine eigenvalue density
accepted_units.why_material: Expands the xi product at conjugate unit-circle boundary points and reduces it to the log-sine expression used for zero-marked density spikes.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the source's equation-level support for section 4.3.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Dense fraction and phase extraction is fragile; scan verification is required for an exact derivation.

accepted_units.title: Direct and contour normalization of the density
accepted_units.why_material: Checks that the proposed singular density integrates to the required total using zero symmetry and independently ties normalization to the resolvent contour integral.
accepted_units.context_note: The direct integral is said to be checkable in Mathematica; this is computational support, not independently captured output.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy with possible sign/conjugation extraction issues; scan and computation should verify exact details.

accepted_units.title: Lagrange-multiplier route to theta=pi*u(h)
accepted_units.why_material: Adds a multiplier enforcing Young-density constraints, varies a positive-factor representation of h, and selects a sign-dependent multiplier to motivate the theta=pi*u(h) identification.
accepted_units.context_note: The main text explicitly calls this heuristic and unproved; the appendix argues constraint compatibility rather than a rigorous uniqueness theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation-dependent and extraction-risky, especially signs, reciprocals, and the final pi factor; scan verification is necessary.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Inverse-design chain from xi symmetry to a zero-sensitive matrix model
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source composes completion symmetry, a critical-line-to-circle map, a log-xi resolvent, boundary-value extraction, and Li Fourier couplings so mapped zeros appear simultaneously as density singularities and force jumps.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The chosen resolvent is nonunique, exact formulas are extraction-sensitive, and its asserted inside-disk analyticity and unit-circle zero placement are explicitly RH-conditional.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Character/eigenvalue duality as a phase-space construction
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Frobenius auxiliary variables obey the eigenvalue saddle and reproduce the eigenvalue partition function at large N; the real saddle supplies a redundant Young boundary, topology constrains it, and a complex Omega packages density and potential marginals.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The paper does not solve the full generic dominant Young density, and the theta=pi*u(h) step remains heuristic.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Zero droplet to prime-counting phase-space analogy
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The same resolvent admits a zero-marked Young-droplet description and a prime-counting-fluctuation integral; non-injectivity in both variables motivates a correspondence between Young and prime-counting branches.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source reports resemblance and a canonical-transform suggestion, not an established symplectic map or a proof that primes and zeros form conjugate variables.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Li positivity is conditional reformulation, not independent RH proof
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Within the designed unit-circle resolvent, Li coefficients become Fourier data and then a manifestly nonnegative sum of 1-cos(n theta_i).
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Earlier steps assume RH to put all nontrivial zeros on the circle and ensure resolvent analyticity, so the source-grounded chain does not furnish an assumption-free proof of RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Internal checks for the spike density
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The main-text density mechanism is backed by an appendix product-to-log-sine derivation and both direct-integral and contour normalization checks.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source mentions a Mathematica check without preserving computational output, and the extracted equations need scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Nonuniqueness at three levels
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: An even-function boundary redundancy is narrowed by droplet topology but still leaves multiple monotone Young branches for the spiky density; the proposed density-to-Young identification supplies only a heuristic selector.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: No uniqueness theorem or complete classification of dominant representations is given.
